title: Man's family want answers in postpolice custody death
article: The former stepfather of the man who died after spending some time in RCMP custody last weekend said his son was a "troubled soul."
Scot Ferguson-Barber said 37year-old Jeremy Richardson lapsed into a coma but was surrounded by his family when he died at Victoria's Royal Jubilee Hospital on Sunday, April 22.
"I understand he had some substance abuse problems," Barber said from Ontario on Thursday. "I know he was a troubled soul."
Richardson's loved ones are now trying to piece together just what happened.
Oak Bay Police were in town Monday, to investigate Richardson's death the day after he was held in North Cowichan/ Duncan RCMP jail cells.
That detachment's officers picked Richardson up after receiving a complaint he was passed out in a public area of downtown Duncan.
Richardson had refused help from paramedics prior to that and was arrested for causing a disturbance and put in Duncan's jail cells to sober up.
But things took a turn for the worse about 2 p.m., police said, when an on-duty guard found the man in medical distress.
An ambulance was called and paramedics took him to Cowichan District Hospital but he was later transferred to Royal Jubilee hospital in Victoria, where he died just before noon on April 22.
The investigation is standard procedure, police say.

"In keeping with the RCMP's commitment to external review of such cases, the Oak Bay Police Service will conduct a review of the circumstances related to this death. The BC Coroners Service are also conducting an investigation, standard in cases where a death occurs in close proximity to a period of police custody."
Oak Bay Police Chief Const. Mark Fisher said the timeline for the investigation depends on what is found.
"It all depends on the circumstances," he said.
